newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seen starting full probe into BT-MCI alliance.
newsitem.headline: EU seen starting full probe into BT-MCI alliance.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to launch a full investigation into the alliance between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Corp. later this week, EU sources said Wednesday.
"There is every chance that the deal will go into the second phase (of investigation)," a commission official told Reuters. The official declined to give any further details.

The planned $20 billion merger between the two telecommunications giants was submitted to the commission for clearance in December under the EU's merger rules, which ban creation or strengthening of dominant positions.

The commission has until Thursday to decide whether to clear it after its preliminary inquiry or launch an in-depth probe if it is worried about the impact on fair competition in Europe. Such an investigation could last up to four months.
BT's Brussels office was not aware of the Commission's decision, but expressed little surprise at the prospect of a thorough investigation into its agreement with MCI.
"We are not picking up any negative vibes about the merger...but there may be some nervousness because it is just so big," BT's EU affairs official Mike Corkerry said.

The Commission has in the past started full probes into megamergers mainly because it needed more time to assess them. That happened last year to the alliance between Sandoz and Ciba-Geigy, which eventually was approved.
BT and MCI announced in November they were pooling their operations into their existing joint venture Concert.
